ann_32.text: On its own, for a typical patient, this part changes the predicted risk only slightly: typical angina, ST depression and resting blood pressure each leave it at about 15% (on the training data only).

Through it, more ST depression clearly raises the predicted risk more if the ST segment does not slope up at peak exercise (from about 51% to about 85%, against about 13% to about 21% with an upsloping ST segment).
Higher resting blood pressure clearly raises it if the ST segment does not slope up (from about 55% to about 77%), but leaves it at about 15% with an upsloping ST segment.
More ST depression clearly raises it more for patients without typical angina (from about 13% to about 21%, against about 2% to about 4% with typical angina).
Chest pain on exercise and the ST slope on their own change it only slightly here, and resting blood pressure raises it only slightly, and only for patients without typical angina.

For patients with an upsloping ST segment, resting blood pressure adds risk only once it rises above about 180 mm Hg, and only slightly (7 patients; the model has little data on this; on the training data only).

ann_33.text: This part acts on 132 of 242 training patients (55%), and 83 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 60-year-old man with 1 vessel coloured, a flat ST segment, 1.0 mm of ST depression, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy and a reversible thallium defect), it slightly lowers the predicted risk, from about 99% to about 98% (on the training data only).

Through it, older age (42 to 66 years) lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 17% to about 8%, and having any chest pain type rather than no chest pain symptoms raises it from about 15% to about 24% (on the training data only).
For patients without chest pain on exercise, age lowers the predicted risk here only once it rises above about 60 years, and only slightly (on the training data only).
Chest pain brought on by exercise raises it only slightly through this part, from about 15% to about 18% (on the training data only).
Whether exercise brings on chest pain changes the effects of age and of chest pain type only slightly.

ann_34.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain (about 3% each) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 15%), and a higher one with a reversible thallium defect (about 41%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 15% to about 95%, a flat ST segment raises it to about 55%, higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) from about 8% to about 34%, and more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) from about 13% to about 21% (on the training data only).

Being a woman lowers it to about 1%, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 4%, and a maximum heart rate of 175 rather than 118 beats per minute from about 20% to about 13% (on the training data only).
Atypical angina lowers it only slightly, to about 11%.
A thallium result coded 4 raises it to about 95% (2 patients; the model has little data on this).
Resting blood pressure changes it only slightly overall (on the training data only), and the model ignores the resting ECG.

ann_32.original: EXERTIONAL-ISCHAEMIA HINGE. Node 855 = ReLU(1.055*trestbps + 0.896*oldpeak + 0.850*exang:1 - 1.358*cp:1 - 0.937*slope:1 - 0.802) is a sparse ischaemia score: high resting BP, ST depression and exercise-induced angina push it up; typical angina (cp:1) and upsloping ST (slope:1) push it down. Node 1501 = ReLU(0.393 - 1.428*855) is its clipped complement. Read out together (+1.300*855 + 0.814*1501) they form a hinge: contribution = 0.320 + 0.138*855 while 855 < 0.276, and 1.300*855 above. So below threshold these five features have almost no effect (effective slopes ~0.12-0.19), and above it they act with full weight (trestbps +1.37, oldpeak +1.17, exang:1 +1.11, slope:1 -1.22, cp:1 -1.77 per SD). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 855 active 36% (mean 0.75, max 7.9); 1501 saturated at 0.393 whenever 855=0; mean 855 is 0.23 without vs 1.78 with exercise angina; positive rate 80% when 855 active vs 24% when zero. Sensitivity of 855: cp:1 0.49, trestbps 0.38, slope:1 0.34, oldpeak 0.32, exang:1 0.31. Ablation (local, readout replaced by train mean): AUC 0.947->0.926, accuracy 0.897->0.847, the largest nonlinear effect in the network.
ann_32.proposed: Through this part, ST depression and higher resting blood pressure raise the predicted risk mainly when the ST segment does not slope up at peak exercise, and ST depression less so with typical angina.

ann_33.original: AGE / NO-ANGINA / CP:4 DAMPING CHAIN. Serial ReLU chain: 1958 = ReLU(1.049*age + 0.061) passes age above about the mean; 1669 = ReLU(1.104*1958 + 1.460*exang:0 - 0.916) is active exactly when there is NO exercise-induced angina (100% of exang:0 cases, 0% otherwise) and grows with age; 3353 = ReLU(1.089*1669 + 0.813*cp:4 - 0.234) adds asymptomatic chest pain. It is read out with -0.515, so it LOWERS risk. Effect: (1) for cp:4 patients (always active) it trims the direct +1.213 cp:4 weight to a net +0.79; (2) for older patients without exertional angina it subtracts up to ~0.65 per SD of age, reversing the small direct +0.236 age effect in that subgroup, and adds ~-0.82 per SD on exang:0. Reading: an asymptomatic-chest-pain patient who is older but does NOT get angina on exercise is less likely diseased than cp:4 alone suggests. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 3353 active 54.5% (100% with cp:4, 18% otherwise); mean readout -0.77 for cp:4 & no exertional angina, -0.35 for cp:4 & angina, -0.09 for no cp:4 & no angina, 0 otherwise. Sensitivity of 3353: exang:0 0.45, cp:4 0.44, age 0.26. Ablation (local, readout replaced by train mean): AUC 0.947->0.945, accuracy 0.897->0.888: a minor correction (logit SD 0.34 vs 3.9 for the linear part).
ann_33.proposed: A part that acts on about half the patients; through it, older age lowers the predicted risk and any chest pain type other than no symptoms raises it.

ann_34.original: ROOT: HEART-DISEASE LOGIT. p = sigmoid(z) (get_formula prints ReLU at the output, but the model applies a sigmoid for this binary task). z = -0.796 + LINEAR CORE + 1.300*855 + 0.814*1501 - 0.515*3353, an additive composition. (1) LINEAR CORE: 16 direct input edges; largest weights ca +2.09, sex:1 +1.42, cp:4 +1.21, slope:2 +1.06, chol +0.76, thal:7 +0.66, cp:2 +0.58, fbs:0 +0.52, thal:4 +0.42; small negative terms exang:1 -0.33, thalach -0.20, exang:0 -0.15. Logit SD 3.94. (2) exertional_ischaemia_hinge (855/1501): a hinge on an ischaemia score (trestbps, oldpeak, exang:1 up; cp:1, slope:1 down) that is nearly flat below threshold and adds risk steeply above it (logit SD 1.64). (3) age_noangina_cp4_chain (1958->1669->3353): a risk-lowering correction that tempers the cp:4 weight and makes age protective for older patients without exertional angina (logit SD 0.34). Eight inputs (cp:3, fbs:1, restecg:0/1/2, slope:3, thal:3, thal:6) are unconnected. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): AUC 0.947, accuracy 0.897. Mean |SHAP| (probability): ca 0.162, sex:1 0.106, slope:2 0.094, cp:4 0.088, thal:7 0.056, chol 0.043, oldpeak 0.042. Ablation ladder (child readout replaced by train mean): linear core only AUC 0.924 / acc 0.851; without hinge 0.926 / 0.847; without chain 0.945 / 0.888. So the network is mostly logistic regression plus one meaningful nonlinear ischaemia hinge and a minor damping chain.
ann_34.proposed: Typical angina and non-anginal chest pain lower the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms. A reversible thallium defect, more vessels coloured, a flat ST segment, higher cholesterol and more ST depression raise it; being a woman, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL and a higher maximum heart rate lower it. The model ignores the resting ECG.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk about 15%), the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain (about 3% each), and a higher one with a reversible defect on the thallium scan (about 41%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 15% to about 95%, and a flat rather than upsloping ST segment at peak exercise raises it to about 55% (on the training data only).

More ST depression on exercise raises the predicted risk, and even more so if the ST segment does not slope up at peak exercise: going from 0 to 2.8 mm clearly moves it from about 51% to about 85% in that case, against about 13% to about 21% with an upsloping ST segment.

Higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg) clearly raises the predicted risk if the ST segment does not slope up (from about 55% to about 77%), but leaves it at about 15% with an upsloping ST segment.
Being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 15% to about 1%, and higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) raises it from about 8% to about 34% (on the training data only).

Worth checking: the model ignores the resting ECG.

ann_32.text: A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than an upsloping ST segment: for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 51% to about 85% if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than an upsloping ST segment, and from about 13% to about 21% if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise.

A higher resting blood pressure clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than an upsloping ST segment: for a typical patient, resting blood pressure going from 110 mm Hg to 155 mm Hg moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 55% to about 77% if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than an upsloping ST segment, and from about 15% to about 15% if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise.

A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if chest pain type is something other than typical angina: for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 13% to about 21% if chest pain type is something other than typical angina, and from about 2% to about 4% if the patient has typical angina.

This changes the prediction only slightly: for a typical patient, resting blood pressure going from 110 mm Hg to 155 mm Hg moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 15% to about 15% if chest pain type is something other than typical angina, and from about 3% to about 3% if the patient has typical angina.

Through this part, resting blood pressure only slightly adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 180 mm Hg for patients with an upsloping ST segment: for a typical such patient, going from 94 mm Hg to 164 mm Hg moves it from about 2% to about 2% (on the training data only). The model has little data on this: only 7 training patients (of them, patients already past their fold).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a slightly higher predicted risk of heart disease if the patient has typical angina (about 15%) than if chest pain type is something other than typical angina (about 15%) (on the training data only).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a slightly higher predicted risk of heart disease if exercise brings on chest pain (about 15%) than if exercise does not bring on chest pain (about 15%).

Through this part, for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 15% to about 15% (on the training data only).
